# sync

Fetches a git remote, lands main's unpublished changes onto its head (those the remote holds already are dropped), moves main there and pushes it; with mode local it pushes nothing. A conflict is E\_CONFLICT with the report a land gives, and nothing moves.

```yaml
title: "sync"
description: "Sync with a git remote."
since: "0.2.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
cli_command: "swarmops sync"
envelope_op: "sync"
request_type: "SyncReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":true,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `SyncReq`: `swarmops schema SyncReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_attempts` | integer | no | `8` | How many times to fetch and land again when the remote or `main` moved meanwhile: 1 to 32. |
| `mode` | string | no | `"publish"` | `publish` (the default) pushes; `local` stops before the push. Whether `sync` sends what it landed. |
| `remote` | string | yes |  | The remote, by its name. |

## Annotations

It lands main's unpublished changes onto a git remote's head, moves main there and pushes. Run again after the remote moved, it lands again. It reaches the remote, beyond the store.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `false` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `true` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops sync`](../commands/sync.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `sync`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops sync`](../commands/sync.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `SyncReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required): the server runs with no identity.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops sync`](../commands/sync.md#errors) lists them.
